items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I took lessons from Barney Bigard.

ctx.x: How long did you play clarinet?
Didn’t play. I just took some lessons. I took lessons from Barney Bigard.
How long did you take lessons?

items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: So he sent me to Barney Bigard. ... So I went to see Barney Bigard, and he gave me a little book, and I started figuring out them notes ... So I worked with him for about what...about three months

ctx.x: The changes. And three chords, C-F-G. But in the meantime, I had been around my uncle Paul between his visits from Chicago, and my uncle Louis and them, and they all got this drum set up, and they'd play... All of them played the drums. So I could get by on the drums, too. They showed me how to hold the sticks properly and they let me play. And my aunt had bought a victrola, and they'd go borrow the victrola in (?), and they'd play against the victrola. And they'd let me play. Then I thought about all them drums…

So my Uncle Paul has got a clarinet. He's foolin' around with the clarinet. Can't play it. He's foolin' around, but he's learning to... I found out later that he was learning so he could count, count notation to write, because he wanted to write. So he figured he'd play a little melody and he'd be able to. So he let me blow the clarinet. A lift-off(?) point. He told me, 'Go take some lessons.'
